newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Sa Sa International eyes expansion in Asia.
newsitem.headline: HK's Sa Sa International eyes expansion in Asia.

text.p: Hong Kong cosmestics products wholesaler and retailer Sa Sa International Holdings Ltd said it planned to expand its retail distribution network in the region.

"We plan to open five more outlets in Hong Kong this year, two more in Taiwan," Sa Sa's chairman Simon Kwok told a news briefing on Monday. "We expect there will have 15 to 20 outlets in Taiwan by the year 2000."

Sa Sa International is engaged in the retail and wholesale of a wide range of cosmetic products including skin-care, make-up, fragrances and hair care products. It operates a chain of 11 retail outlets in Hong Kong and one shop in Taipei.
Kwok said the company would open an outlet in Macau in July and one in Singapore later in November.
The company will hold a distribution joint venture with a Japanese cosmetics distribution group Nikonikodo Inc to distribute cosmetics products in Japan, Kwok said.
"We are planning to establish outlets in Tokyo and Osaka later this year before we expand further into Korea and Malaysia in next two to three years," Kwok added.
Sa Sa said earlier it would issue a total 328 million new shares, or 25 percent of its enlarged share capital, in a flotation.
Of the total, 65.6 million shares will be offered to the public in Hong Kong, with the balance of 262.40 million shares for international placement.

The shares will be issued at a price ranging from HK$2.00 to HK$2.38 per share, giving a price to earnings multiple of 11.6 to 13.8 times on a weighted average basis, and 11.8 to 14.0 times on a fully diluted basis.
"The (cosmetics) market potential is huge in Asia. the market is far from saturation," said Peter Tong, executive director of the company.
According to a survey, Asian women were estimated to have spent US$32 billion on cosmetics in 1996 and the market was seen growing by another 24 percent by the year 2001, Tong said.
Sa Sa forecast profit after taxation and minority interests but before extraordinary items of not less than HK$215 million for the year ending in March 1998.

It posted profit of HK$157.93 million for the year ended in March 1997, up from HK$115.20 million in 1996 and HK$51.82 million in 1995. Turnover rose to HK$990.45 million in 1997, from HK$741.27 million in 1996 and HK$487.40 million in 1995.
The Hong Kong public offering will run from June 3 to 6 and dealing in shares is expected to begin on June 13.
